years_searched: Every year from 1899 to 1918 and 1924 to 1972 is covered by the state accident registers. 1919 to 1923 comes from local newspaper reports and is not complete. For 1869 to 1898 the names come from the inspectors' yearly reports and genealogy transcriptions, which are complete for most Northumberland County years but have gaps elsewhere.

known_but_unnamed.text: The state mine inspector counted 7 dead from the boiler house explosion, but newspapers name only 6. The seventh was probably one of the men reported fatally hurt: fireman J. F. Dichanettie (the name is unclear in the scan) or laborer Peter Heck.

The Shenandoah Evening Herald of September 4, 1897 reports a boy from Shenandoah killed that morning while riding down the slope of the Suffolk colliery in a car. The part of the page that gave his name is not readable in the scan.

The Shenandoah Evening Herald of October 18, 1892, reporting the death of miner Lawrence Burns at Gilberton, says his brother had been killed at the Elmwood colliery about two years before. The brother's first name is not given.
